Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced on 13 November 2026 that the newly constructed six-lane Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur Bridge over the Ganga River will be named ‘Nitish Setu’ , after former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar . Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the bridge on 21 November 2026. Key Points: Naming of the Bridge: The Bihar government has named the Kachchi Dargah-Raghopur-Bidupur six-lane bridge as ‘Nitish Setu’ in recognition of Nitish Kumar's contribution to the state's development. The announcement was made by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on 13 November 2026. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will dedicate the bridge to the nation during his Bihar visit on 21 November 2026. Geographical Connectivity: The bridge has been constructed across the Ganga River , connecting Kachchi Dargah in Patna district with Bidupur in Vaishali district through Raghopur. It will strengthen connectivity between North and South Bihar . It is expected to reduce traffic congestion on the existing Mahatma Gandhi Setu. The main bridge is approximately 9.76 km long , while its total length, including approach roads, is around 19.76 km. Project Background: The foundation stone of the project was laid by Nitish Kumar in August 2015 . The first phase, connecting Kachchi Dargah with Raghopur Diara, was opened to traffic on 23 June 2025 . The project has been developed as a major road infrastructure link for the Patna–Vaishali region. Significance of the Project: Improved connectivity is expected to facilitate movement between Patna and districts of North Bihar. It will support regional economic activities and improve access to markets and public services. It is also expected to provide an alternative route to reduce pressure on existing road bridges across the Ganga. national_raw_news.title: Improved infrastructure and business environment make India attractive destination for Japanese ...
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar has called for strengthening India-Japan cooperation in key areas, including economic security, advanced manufacturing, semiconductors, critical minerals, clean energy and defence. Addressing the inaugural event of Raisina Tokyo 2026, Dr Jaishankar said the rapidly changing global landscape has made trusted partnerships, supply chain diversification and stronger national capacities increasingly important. Dr Jaishankar said India and Japan, as leading nations of the Indo-Pacific committed to a free and open region, must deepen reliable cooperation while safeguarding their national interests and promoting regional stability. Mr Jaishankar said the transformation of India, particularly since 2014, has improved the country’s infrastructure, business environment and manufacturing potential, making it an increasingly attractive destination for Japanese investment and production. He also highlighted India’s progress in education, skill development, innovation and start-ups, citing opportunities for cooperation in digital technology, space, drones, healthcare and defence. The Minister identified artificial intelligence, pharmaceuticals, information and communication technology and clean energy among the areas offering greater scope for bilateral collaboration. Calling for stronger people-to-people ties, he stressed the need to expand exchanges in education, culture and language. Dr Jaishankar outlined five defining features of the current global landscape- repeated shocks to the international system, weaponisation and strategic chokepoints, extreme competition and greater risk-taking, de-risking and diversification, and the growing importance of trusted partnerships. Dr Jaishankar said India and Japan are members of the Quad, partners in the G4 initiative for United Nations reform and participants in the East Asia Summit. He said stronger India-Japan ties would contribute to stability and security in the Indo-Pacific and strengthen the foundations of a multipolar Asia and a multipolar world.

national_raw_news.title: Women’s Asian Champions hockey tournament begins tomorrow in Bhopal: 6 teams, including India in fray 4 hours ago 82
national_raw_news.content: The Women’s Asian Champions Trophy 2026 hockey tournament will begin in Bhopal tomorrow. The tournament will continue till 28th of this month. Apart from India, teams from China, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia and Thailand will participate in the tournament. India has won this title three times in 2016, 2023 and 2024. India will begin its campaign against Malaysia tomorrow. The match will start at 7 PM. Recently, the Indian women’s hockey team defeated China to win the gold medal at the 2026 Asian Games after 44 years. With this victory, the team also qualified for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The Asian Champions Trophy will be country’s first international tournament after its Asian Games victory. All six teams will play against each other in the league stage. Each team will play five matches, and the top four teams in the points table will qualify for the semi-finals. League matches will be held from 19th to 25th September. Both semi-finals and the match for fifth place will take place on 27th of this month. The bronze medal match and the final will be played on 28th of this month. India will face South Korea on 21st November, Thailand on 22nd, and China on 24th November. The Indian team will play its final league match against Japan on 25th November.

national_raw_news.title: Ayushman Bharat reflects country’s commitment to making quality healthcare affordable to all: VP Radhakrishnan 37 mins ago 10
national_raw_news.content: Vice President CP Radhakrishnan has said that a healthy, educated and empowered population would form the foundation of country’s national progress. He emphasised that a Viksit Bharat must also be a Swasth Bharat. He was addressing the eight Convocation of Vardhman Mahavir Medical College and Safdarjung Hospital in New Delhi this evening. The Vice President said that initiatives such as Ayushman Bharat reflect the country’s commitment to making quality healthcare accessible and affordable to all. He has called upon young doctors to uphold compassion, empathy and human dignity in patient care. He said, no scientific advancement can replace the human touch between a doctor and a patient. Mr Radhakrishnan also urged the graduating doctors to keep the nation first in all their thoughts and actions, invoking the principle of Rashtra Pratham. He said doctors are among the most respected citizens because of the trust and responsibility placed in them by society. He encouraged them to uphold the ideals of compassion, humanity and selfless service inspired by Lord Mahavira. Speaking on this occasion, Health and Family Welfare Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda said that medical education in the country has expanded significantly over the last 12 years. He said that number of AIIMS in the country has reached to 23. Mr Nadda said the expansion of medical education is being accompanied by a focus on maintaining quality. He also highlighted the government’s aim to add 75 thousand undergraduate and postgraduate medical seats by 2029.

national_raw_news.title: Elections 73 Uttar Pradesh publishes draft electoral roll for 2027 Assembly polls with 13.58 crore voters
national_raw_news.content: Uttar Pradesh’s draft electoral roll for the 2027 Assembly elections has been published. It comprises 13.58 crore voters after a net addition of 18.84 lakh electorates during the Special Summary Revision (SSR). UP Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Navdeep Rinwa said, the draft roll updates the previous final list released on April 10, 2026, after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). Out of a total of 13.58 crore voters, Men account for 7.38 crore, while Women account for 6.20 crore, reflecting an addition of nearly 11 lakh female electors since the April 2026 roll. The roll includes 4,042 third-gender electors. Citizens in the 18-19 age group represent 11.83 lakh of the total voters. The revision is being conducted with January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date for eligible citizens turning 18. Eligible residents can file their claims and objections from November 17 to December 16, 2026. Citizens can use Form 6 for new voter inclusion, Form 7 for deletion of names, and Form 8 for correcting existing entries. Election officials will resolve all submitted claims and objections by December 28, 2026. The final electoral roll will be published on January 4, 2027. Voters can inspect the roll at all 1,73,730 polling booths across the state’s 403 Assembly constituencies in 75 districts, or check their status online via the CEO Uttar Pradesh Portal.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi returns to New Delhi after a successful two-day visit to Philippines
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi returned to New Delhi after successfully concluding his two-day visit to Manila, the Philippines. During the visit, Mr Modi participated in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit, the 21st East Asia Summit and the Quad Leaders’ Meeting. Prime Minister also visited the historic Gurudwara Khalsa Diwan in Manila and took part in the ceremony marking the commencement of its redevelopment. Mr Modi also met Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., and the two leaders discussed ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in defence, security, trade and investment. The prime minister also discussed regional and global issues of mutual interest with his counterparts from Singapore and Thailand on the sidelines of the visit. At the annual ASEAN-India summit, the prime minister proposed nine initiatives, including a long-term maritime plan to boost connectivity and ensure seafarers’ security, free e-visas for tourists from the bloc’s member nations, cooperation on mining and critical minerals, and a framework for technical exchanges in the civil nuclear energy sector. In his remarks, Modi underlined the importance New Delhi attaches to its comprehensive strategic partnership with ASEAN and affirmed the two sides should work for peace, stability and predictability in the region and beyond. At the Quad Summit, Mr Modi said for India, the Quad is a “constructive and trusted” partnership that strives to deliver trusted solutions across the Indo-Pacific, spanning maritime security, supply chains, new technologies, and disaster response. The Quad is a strategic grouping of India, the US, Japan and Australia that works to promote a free, open and inclusive Indo-Pacific through cooperation on maritime security, technology, infrastructure and regional stability. During his address at the 21st East Asia Summit (EAS), Mr Modi announced the launch of a seafarers’ safety initiative to boost joint training and emergency response among EAS nations, emphasising that safeguarding maritime security and freedom of navigation is essential to protecting the seas as a lifeline of shared prosperity. ASEAN is a regional grouping comprising 11 Southeast Asian countries — Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Cambodia and Timor-Leste. India, along with the US, China, Japan and Australia, is among its dialogue partners.

national_raw_news.content: The Quad leaders have announced a series of initiatives to strengthen maritime security, artificial intelligence cooperation, cybersecurity and critical infrastructure connectivity across the Indo-Pacific at the Manila Summit in the Philippines. The summit brought together Prime Minister Narendra Modi, US President Donald Trump, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. In a joint press release, the four leaders reaffirmed their commitment to a free, open, safe and prosperous Indo-Pacific, describing the Quad as a “partnership of action” dedicated to peace, stability and prosperity. The meeting also marked nearly a decade since the revival of the Quad and the 10th anniversary of the vision of a Free and Open Indo-Pacific, first articulated by the late Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe in 2016. The leaders strongly opposed destabilising or unilateral actions aimed at changing the status quo through force or coercion, saying such actions escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability. They also expressed grave concern over economic coercion, including arbitrary export restrictions. Emphasising the importance of resilient supply chains, freedom of navigation and overflight, and the use of emerging technologies, the leaders committed to working together to ensure open, safe and resilient maritime transit corridors across the Indo-Pacific. The four countries announced the inaugural Quad Business Leaders’ Forum, scheduled to be held in early 2027. The forum will bring together business leaders, government officials and policy experts from the four countries to strengthen private-sector engagement, promote commercial deals and develop partnerships that contribute to the prosperity of the Indo-Pacific.

national_raw_news.title: Northern Railway facilitates travel of 1.82 crore passengers during festive season 2 hours ago 25
national_raw_news.content: Northern Railway has successfully facilitated the travel of nearly 1.82 crore passengers during Puja and the festive season this year. It registered an increase of around 10 lakh passengers compared to the corresponding period last year. Through strategic capacity enhancement, an expanded fleet of special trains, coach augmentations, and continuous demand monitoring, the zone significantly outperformed its previous year’s operational benchmarks. According to the Northern Railway, seven thousand 85 special train trips were operated during the festive season of Diwali and Chhath Puja, compared to four thousand 666 trips last year. This means around 54 additional special train trips were operated every day to manage the festive rush. Daily passenger handling also increased from approximately 3 lakh 91 thousand to 4 lakh 14 thousand, accommodating nearly 22 thousand 700 additional passengers every day. Of the total passengers carried, around 1 crore 66 lakh travelled through regular train services, while 12 lakh 83 thousand were accommodated through special Trains on Demand services. To maximise capacity on high-demand routes, Northern Railway added 581 coaches to regular trains this year, while 123 coaches were added during the corresponding period last year, which shows an increase of approximately 372 percent this time around. By combining proactive fleet expansion with real-time crowd and demand monitoring, Northern Railway ensured reliable connectivity and enhanced comfort for millions of festive travellers across its network.

national_raw_news.content: New Delhi: 3rd DHR-ICMR Health Research Excellence Summit brings together over 600 scientists, researchers, policymakers Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर New Delhi: 3rd DHR-ICMR Health Research Excellence Summit brings together over 600 scientists, researchers, policymakers ANI | Updated: Nov 18, 2026 14:28 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 18 (ANI): The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has achieved the milestone of 100 successful technology transfer deals, marking a significant step in translating indigenous health research into technologies and solutions for wider public use. The milestone was announced at the 3rd Department of Health Research (DHR)-ICMR Health Research Excellence Summit, which concluded today at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Organised by DHR and ICMR on 16 and 17 November 2026, the two-day Summit brought together over 600 scientists, researchers, innovators, administrators and policymakers from ICMR institutes, partner institutions, government organisations and academia. The Summit also marked 115 years of ICMR's contribution to biomedical and health research in the country, according to a press release issued by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. The Summit serves as a national platform for recognising excellence in health research and promoting the translation of scientific evidence into tangible outcomes. It showcases significant contributions from ICMR institutes and extramural partner institutions across research publications, technologies, patents and research management, while facilitating collaboration among researchers, industry and policymakers. At the Technology Transfer Ceremony, ICMR exchanged 20 licensing agreements covering eight technologies with nine Indian companies, taking the cumulative number of successful technology transfer deals to 100 within a limited time of less than 2 years of Medical Innovations Patent Mitra, a flagship initiative of ICMR launched by Union Health and Family Welfare Minister, Shri J P Nadda, in March 2025. This milestone reflects ICMR's continued efforts to facilitate the translation of research and indigenous innovations into practical applications through industry partnerships. As per the release, an Innovation Exhibition showcased 17 technologies developed by ICMR institutes and extramural partner institutions. In addition, 10 technologies and eight patents were presented during a dedicated session on Technologies and Patents, highlighting the breadth of innovation emerging from the country's health research ecosystem. Three new initiatives were launched at the Summit. The DHR’s new Research to Action Vertical will translate research evidence into decision-ready products for policy and programmes. Syndromic Surveillance under the DHR Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories (VRDL) Scheme will create an early-warning network for outbreaks across 70 VRDLs and Infectious Disease Research & Diagnostic Laboratories (IRDLs). The Dr M K Bhan Young Medical Faculty PhD Portal launched today will serve as a centralised digital platform with information for prospective applicants, the release said. ICMR also released the Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) Annual Report and Standard Operating Procedures, bringing together the national evidence base on antimicrobial resistance and standardised laboratory procedures. The ICMR Compendium, featuring 25 stories of research translated into outcomes for people, was also released. national_raw_news.title: Union Sports Minister Mandaviya calls for integrated national sports ecosystem built around ...
national_raw_news.content: Union Sports Minister Mandaviya calls for integrated national sports ecosystem built around universities Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Union Sports Minister Mandaviya calls for integrated national sports ecosystem built around universities ANI | Updated: Nov 18, 2026 14:19 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 18 (ANI): Union Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports Mansukh Mandaviya, chaired a meeting with 13 Sports Universities from across India, in New Delhi on Wednesday. The discussions revolved around strengthening collaboration among Sports Universities, sharing expertise and resources, and building an integrated ecosystem to enhance India’s sports education, research, training, and global competitiveness, as per a press release from the Union Youth Affairs and Sports Ministry. Dr Mandaviya said, “Our vision is to make Sports Universities the hub of the entire sports ecosystem, where athletes, coaches, training, research, competitions, and world-class infrastructure are all developed together.” The Union Sports Minister encouraged all universities to develop their own expertise in particular sports to benefit the country. “Every university needs to develop its own specific expertise – whether in a particular sport, coaching, sports science, or research. This will benefit the entire nation,” he said. While the Minister envisioned that the universities develop their own niche areas of expertise, he also encouraged them to partake in knowledge-sharing with each other. “We will no longer work in silos. By integrating our efforts, resources, and expertise, we will build a strong, collaborative national sports ecosystem,” said Dr. Mandaviya. “Every Coach exchange, knowledge exchange, and resource sharing among universities will be promoted. Despite the fact that a major part of the focus remains on furthering the capabilities of India’s athletes, Dr. Mandaviya also encouraged the universities to build systems that would help India grow its sporting ecosystem and industry as a whole. “Universities must focus on developing specialised expertise in emerging sectors such as Sports Science, Sports Law, and Sports Tourism, to develop skilled professionals and strong institutional capabilities in these fields across India,” said Dr Mandaviya. “Sports Universities must not limit themselves to just athletes, but also develop sports professionals who can contribute to sports management, administration, and the overall sports ecosystem,” he further stated. “Our goal is for Indian Sports Universities to make their mark at the global level and establish their place among the world's leading universities.” The meeting was attended by Hon’ble Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports, Raksha Khadse, Secretary (Sports) Hari Ranjan Rao, and Vice-Chancellors and other representatives from 13 Sports Universities across the country. national_raw_news.title: Lonar Lake in Maharashtra finds place in 'Third 100 IUGS Geological Heritage Sites'
national_raw_news.content: Lonar Lake in Maharashtra finds place in 'Third 100 IUGS Geological Heritage Sites' | Mathrubhumi English Home page » Technology » Science » Geological Heritage Lonar Lake in Maharashtra finds place in 'Third 100 IUGS Geological Heritage Sites' # PTI Last Updated: 18 November 2026, 02:47 PM IST Follow us on Nagpur: Lonar Lake, a meteorite-impact crater located in the Buldhana district of Maharashtra, has been included in the prestigious list of the 'Third 100 IUGS Geological Heritage Sites'. The International Union of Geological Sciences (IUGS) recognises Geological Heritage Sites for their outstanding scientific value as exceptional examples of geological features, processes, and discoveries, a release issued by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) said. They represent some of the world's most significant places for understanding the Earth and its history. Located across the globe, they offer a surprising journey through the most important geological sites of the Earth. The release said the selection of the 'Third 100' builds on the success and global impact of the 'First 100', announced in Zumaia, Spain, in 2022, and the 'Second 100', announced during the 37th International Geological Congress (IGC 2024) in Busan, Republic of Korea. Since 2022, more than 1,000 experts from 90 countries and 20 international organisations have contributed to this programme by proposing sites, participating in the selection process, and evaluating their scientific quality. With 74 active national members, IUGS is one of the world's largest scientific organisations. It encourages international cooperation and participation in the Earth sciences in relation to human welfare. Lonar Lake crater in Buldhana is one of the youngest (approximately 12,000 years old) and best-preserved bowl-shaped hypervelocity impact structures on Earth. With a diameter of approximately 1.88 km, it is uniquely situated within the extensive Deccan Traps, a succession of tholeiitic continental flood basalts formed around 65 million years ago, according to the release. It is particularly significant as one of the rare terrestrial impact craters formed in basaltic rocks and is considered one of the five known hypervelocity meteorite impact craters on Earth developed in a basaltic target. The crater hosts a saline-alkaline lake at its centre, creating a distinctive geological and ecological setting. Its circular morphology, depth-to-diameter ratio, exposed basaltic lava flows along the inner slopes, brecciated subsurface rocks, outward-dipping country rocks, debris mounds, and extensive ejecta deposits containing fragmented breccia and suevite provide compelling evidence of its meteoritic impact origin, it said. Impact-related materials, including impact glass, spherules, and melt rocks, offer important evidence for understanding the physical and geochemical processes associated with hypervelocity impacts. "The Geological Survey of India (GSI), through its sustained efforts in geoheritage conservation in India, took up the initiative to submit this proposal to IUGS for consideration under this prestigious international initiative," it said.
